analyst_view.overall: Shakhtar (21st, 4 points) host Fenerbahçe (19th, 5 points) at Stamford Bridge in London because of the war, so there is little real home advantage; both need points to stay in play-off contention. Shakhtar, under Arda Turan, are winless in three after failing to beat Lviv on Friday and miss Pedrinho (counted, -14% on their goals), Marlon Gomes (in the numbers' list; one Ukrainian report says he is still out) and young striker Kauã Elias (foot fracture, surgery), whom the numbers don't list. Fenerbahçe, under Emre Belözoğlu, drew 2-2 at Kocaelispor after beating Liverpool 3-2; Turkish reports say Kanté returns to midfield and Muriqi starts up front instead of Lukaku, with Aké (counted), Oosterwolde and Asensio out. English referee Michael Oliver (4.0 cards a game) is named and already counted. My only moves remain small cuts for Elias's absence.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and already take Pedrinho off Shakhtar (-14%) while adding 6% for Aké missing at Fenerbahçe's back. Kauã Elias's foot fracture is not in the numbers, but he has been out since early November, so some of it is already in their form; I trim only a little, to about 2.6. Muriqi replacing Lukaku is a like-for-like swap for Fenerbahçe, so it doesn't move me further.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already raised about 12% for Shakhtar's busy recent corner count and trimmed 9% for Fenerbahçe's. A neutral ground in London takes some of Shakhtar's home push away, but Fenerbahçe's wide players Greenwood and Aktürkoğlu and a target man in Muriqi keep crosses coming, so nothing points clearly either way and I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, a high figure that reflects Fenerbahçe's card-heavy style (about 3 a game) and both sides' records, with referee Michael Oliver near the average at 4.0 a game. Two Turkish coaches with a Galatasaray-Fenerbahçe history and two sides needing points add edge, and Kanté's return adds a ball-winner, but the numbers already carry that style, so I stay at 4.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.4 shots, with Shakhtar's recent shooting run already adding about 15% to their side and Fenerbahçe's trimmed 9%. Elias's loss shows more in finishing than in volume, and Muriqi took two shots in 45 minutes off the bench at the weekend where Lukaku had none, so I stay at about 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Without Kauã Elias, which the numbers don't see, Shakhtar lean more on Alisson Santana and the wide players, who have been wasteful in Europe, so I trim slightly, to about 8.5.
